title: Binary Choice under Asymmetric Loss in a Data-Rich Environment: Theory and an Application to Algorithmic Fairness
reasoning: The paper focuses on the statistical and econometric theory of asymmetric loss functions in binary choice models. While it applies this theory to 'algorithmic fairness' in criminal justice (a topic with ethical implications), its focus is on technical risk-minimization and welfare weights rather than evaluating religion, morals, or religious/theological ethics.
